title: Stochastic GPU pool fencing and tenant latency contracts
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: As Dedicated customers scale, a small number of noisy tenants cause multi-tenant GPU pools to miss inferred latency SLOs and consume disproportionate burst capacity. Current hard-slicing approaches are too rigid for mixed workloads (interactive low-latency + offline batch) and lead to underutilization. We need an approach that provides per-tenant throughput/latency contracts, rapid noisy-neighbor mitigation, and graceful quota enforcement while maintaining high utilization across heterogeneous fleets.

Proposal summary: Implement a stochastic fencing layer above the scheduler that enforces probabilistic tenant caps and latency contracts using burst-credit budgets, sliding fairness windows, and predictive backpressure signals. The system: (1) assigns each tenant a latency contract (p99, target throughput) and a burst credit pool; (2) continuously scores incoming requests by expected GPU work (seq len, batchability, model profile) and an urgency weight; (3) admits, shapes, or redirects requests using a combination of token-bucket shaping, short-term preemption for low-priority batch, and soft-fence evictions for tenants exceeding probabilistic thresholds.

Why different: Unlike rigid hard-slicing or wholesale fractional GPU assignment, stochastic fencing adapts to observed workload distributions and provides explicit latency contracts that can be traded for burst capacity. It aims to keep utilization high by allowing occasional overcommit while bounding tail-latency risk.

Metrics to track: per-tenant p50/p95/p99 latency, admitted throughput, burst-credit balance, eviction rate, preemption count, GPU utilization by pool, number of cross-tenant fallbacks, and customer pain events (support tickets).

Rollout plan (high level): 1) simulation & synthetic workloads (2 weeks) 2) implement fence controller and scoring module (3 weeks) 3) limited rollout to internal tenants + canary customers (2 weeks) 4) observe for 4 weeks, iterate on scoring weights 5) wider opt-in rollout with GUI controls in Console and automatic fallback to today’s lane-based quotas if regressions detected.

Operational considerations: must provide clear observability (per-request tag of fence-decision and score), a Playbook for investigating noisy tenants, and a self-service path for customers to request dedicated slices if they need absolute isolation.

Security/compliance: design keeps tenant data out of scoring (only metadata: seq length, model id, requested tokens, route tier). No model payloads are stored in the fence controller.
acceptance_criteria: Simulation shows p99 of latency for VIP/interactive tenants remains within 1.15x baseline under a mixed workload with 5 noisy tenants
Fence controller accepts scoring inputs and emits admit/shape/preempt decisions with <=2ms median decision latency
Canary deployment with 3 customers shows no more than 10% increase in support tickets vs baseline during first 4 weeks
Console exposes per-tenant burst-credit and a togglable latency-contract UI and audit events are recorded to logs
Automated rollback triggers if pooled GPU p99 exceeds configured SLO for more than 10 minutes
technical_notes: Scoring: model_id -> hardware profile mapping, expected per-token GPU ms estimate, and batchability heuristic
Admission control: hierarchical token-bucket per-tenant with a sliding window fairness adjustment; bucket refill tied to committed throughput and credits
Preemption: implement low-cost checkpoint for multi-request KV cache eviction for preempted batch jobs; prefer batch slowdown over hard kill
Eviction policy: soft fence uses probabilistic eviction scoring (age, credit deficit, interruptibility) to reduce spike-induced impact
Integration: expose fence decisions as headers in the request trace for Console and tracing systems (x-rd-fence-decision)
Scheduler hooks: lightweight admission filter in runtime that can be toggled per pool; avoid hot path if disabled
Persistence: burst-credit ledger persisted to a lightweight key-value store with per-tenant TTLs; ensure idempotency during controller restarts
Compatibility: support both MIG-capable GPUs and full-GPU tenants; for MIG, map MIG slice classes to fence weight multipliers
Safety: emergency hard-slice toggle for SRE to immediately isolate a tenant during incidents

Design review (Maya Chen, 2026-03-02): Console controls need a 'safe default' that prevents accidental aggressive credits; suggested 'recommended' presets for common workload patterns
Security note (Priya Shah, 2026-03-06): Confirmed scoring only uses request metadata; recommended a short privacy audit to sign off on telemetry retention policy

Eng feedback (Ravi Patel, 2026-03-09): Need more detail on preemption path to avoid large KV-cache rebuild costs; proposed lightweight checkpointing and read-only cache reconstruction for preempted requests
SRE comment (Noah Green, 2026-03-12): Add an emergency isolation API so runbooks can quickly flip to hard-slice a tenant during a customer-facing outage
